paragraphs.title: A Call to Praise and Music

easy.explanation: Verse 1 calls the righteous to rejoice in the LORD.
easy.q: Who is called to rejoice in the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Praise the LORD with harp.”
easy.q: What instrument is named for praising the LORD?

easy.explanation: The psalm mentions “the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings.”
easy.q: With what kind of instrument should the LORD be praised?

medium.explanation: The verses call the upright to rejoice, praise, and sing unto the LORD.
medium.q: What are the righteous and upright called to do together?
What does “comely” mean in “for praise is comely for the upright”?

medium.explanation: The loud sound contributes to the joyful and triumphant praise.
medium.q: What does playing with “a loud noise” add to the worship?

answers: Rejoice, praise, and sing a new song
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from rejoicing and praising to singing a new song.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the acts of praise in these verses?

challenge.explanation: A new song suggests renewed and fresh expression of praise to the LORD.
challenge.q: What does “Sing unto him a new song” suggest?

challenge.explanation: The repeated command is to praise and sing unto the LORD.
challenge.q: To whom are the praise and singing directed?

paragraphs.title: The LORD's Integrity and the Creation of the World

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “For the word of the LORD is right.”
easy.q: How is the word of the LORD described?

answers: By the word of the LORD
By the strength of a king
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “By the word of the LORD were the heavens made.”
easy.q: By what were the heavens made?

answers: Gathers them together as an heap
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says that He gathers the waters of the sea together as an heap.
easy.q: What does the LORD do with the waters of the sea?

answers: His word is right and His works are faithful
His word is hidden and His works are weak
His word changes and His works are accidental
medium.explanation: The passage joins the rightness of His word with the truth of all His works.
medium.q: What connection do the verses make between the LORD's word and His works?

answers: The heavenly bodies and their multitude
All the cities of the earth
medium.explanation: In the context of creation, “the host” refers to the heavenly array.
medium.q: What does “all the host of them” refer to?

answers: He created and orders the world
He needs help from the earth
medium.explanation: The verses emphasize His power to create, command, and control the waters and heavens.
medium.q: Why should all the earth fear the LORD?

answers: Creation occurred by His spoken command
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the LORD spoke and commanded, and creation came into being.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “he spake” and “he commanded” emphasize?

answers: The LORD's truth, goodness, creation, and authority
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the LORD's character to His creative power and authority.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in verses 4–9?

answers: His word brings things into being
His word is weaker than nature
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a direct connection between His command and the completed act.
challenge.q: What does “he spake, and it was done” teach about the LORD's power?

paragraphs.title: The LORD's Counsel over Human Plans

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “The LORD bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought.”
easy.q: What does the LORD do to the counsel of the heathen?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever.”
easy.q: How long does the counsel of the LORD stand?

answers: The nation whose God is the LORD
The nation with the largest army
easy.explanation: Verse 12 calls blessed the nation whose God is the LORD and whom He has chosen.

answers: Human plans and the LORD's counsel
medium.explanation: The plans of the nations fail, while the LORD's counsel stands forever.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in this passage?

answers: Makes it fail or come to nothing
medium.explanation: The phrase means to defeat, frustrate, or render ineffective.

answers: The LORD is their God and has chosen them
They are greater than every nation
medium.explanation: Their blessedness is connected with belonging to God and being chosen as His inheritance.
medium.q: Why is the chosen people described as blessed?

answers: The LORD's counsel is more enduring than human plans
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: Human plans are frustrated, but the LORD's counsel stands from generation to generation.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the LORD's counsel and human thoughts show?

challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the continuing permanence of the LORD's counsel.
challenge.q: What does “to all generations” mean in this context?

answers: People are blessed when the LORD is their God and has chosen them
Blessedness depends only on military power
challenge.explanation: The passage connects blessedness with the LORD's relationship to His chosen people.
challenge.q: What relationship does the passage establish between the LORD's rule and the people's blessedness?

easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “The LORD looketh from heaven.”
easy.q: From where does the LORD look upon humanity?

easy.explanation: The verse says that He beholds all the sons of men.
Verse 15 says, “He fashioneth their hearts alike.”
easy.q: What does the LORD fashion alike?

answers: He is present only in cities
medium.explanation: The verse connects His fashioning of their hearts with His knowledge of their works.
medium.q: Why can the LORD consider all the works of people?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the LORD's dwelling place.
medium.q: What does “the place of his habitation” mean?

answers: All the inhabitants of the earth
medium.explanation: The verses repeatedly describe His attention as extending to all people on earth.
medium.q: What is the scope of the LORD's watch in this passage?

answers: The LORD formed the heart and therefore understands the works
The heart has no connection with actions
Only outward actions are known to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The LORD fashioned the hearts of people and considers all their works.
challenge.q: What relationship between the heart and actions is shown in the passage?

answers: The universal scope of the LORD's vision
That He sees only world leaders
That His watch is limited to one place
challenge.explanation: Both expressions broaden the focus to include humanity everywhere.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “all the sons of men” to “all the inhabitants of the earth” emphasize?

answers: He knows both inner character and outward behavior
He does not know human actions
challenge.explanation: The verse presents His knowledge as including both the fashioned heart and all human works.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD seeing both the heart and the works?

answers: Only if he has a horse
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “There is no king saved by the multitude of an host.”
easy.q: Is a king saved by the multitude of an host alone?

answers: The great strength of a mighty man
easy.explanation: The passage rejects confidence in armies, strength, and the horse.
easy.q: What does not guarantee deliverance according to the passage?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “He is our help and our shield.”
easy.q: Who is the help and shield?

answers: Fearing the LORD, hoping in His mercy, and trusting Him
medium.explanation: The passage directs hope toward the LORD's mercy and protection rather than human strength.
medium.q: What does the hope in this passage depend upon?

answers: We hope in and patiently await the LORD
medium.explanation: Waiting for the LORD expresses hope, trust, and patient dependence upon Him.
medium.q: What does “our soul waiteth for the LORD” mean?

answers: Those who fear Him hope in His mercy, and He delivers and preserves them
Fear of the LORD prevents prayer
Fear of the LORD depends on the strength of a horse
medium.explanation: The verses connect fearing the LORD and hoping in His mercy with deliverance from death and famine.
medium.q: What connection is made between fearing the LORD and preserving life?

answers: Trust in human strength versus trust in the LORD's mercy
challenge.explanation: The first verses reject confidence in military power, while the later verses emphasize trusting the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between verses 16–17 and verses 18–22?

answers: They expect and trust in the LORD
challenge.explanation: Their waiting expresses dependence, hope, and confidence in the LORD.
challenge.q: What does “Our soul waiteth for the LORD” reveal about the speakers?

answers: Trust in the LORD brings joy
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 says, “For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.”
challenge.q: Why is the rejoicing of the heart connected with the LORD's holy name?
